build.#: Two scripts for one build. `build:cargo` declares no inputs, so wireit never calls it fresh and cargo is always consulted — cargo tracks its own inputs better than a `files` list could, and a no-op is a quarter of a second. This one names the binary cargo produced as an *input*, so its fingerprint changes exactly when the binary does, and that is what dependents inherit. `cascade: false` keeps `build:cargo`'s own fingerprint out: a script with no `files` is not `fullyTracked`, and wireit propagates that to everything downstream, where nothing can ever be fresh — which is why one `npm test` with no changes used to rebuild the whole bootstrap chain. Hashing the binary also makes freshness imply the binary exists, so the exit-127 case that a `files` list alone would have allowed cannot happen.

build:cargo.#: Always runs; `build` is what dependents read. See its comment.

test.#command: --release reuses the dependency artifacts the build step produced instead of compiling wasmtime a second time in the dev profile.
